en.headline: Police arrest 57 including 14-year-old in triad debt collection crackdown
en.dek: Officers dismantled a triad-controlled syndicate that recruited youths for red-paint attacks and threats, also shutting a brothel, drug den and three illegal gambling dens.
body: Hong Kong police have arrested 57 people aged 14 to 70 in a special operation targeting a triad-controlled illegal debt collection syndicate active across the territory, with further raids closing related illegal premises.

The operation began with an ambush on 13 July in Sau Mau Ping Estate, where a 14-year-old boy was intercepted carrying a bottle of red paint and a knuckle duster. He was arrested on suspicion of possession of anything with intent to destroy or damage property and possession of a prohibited weapon. Core members, including several aged 15 to 18, were arrested in the following days on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage linked to cases in the district.

Between 22 and 28 July officers arrested another 10 people in connection with additional criminal damage and intimidation cases. From 28 to 30 July a joint operation raided five premises, resulting in 41 arrests for offences including operating a vice establishment, keeping a drug den, drug trafficking and consumption, and illegal gambling. Seizures included cocaine, methamphetamine, gambling machines, mahjong and poker tables, about HK$40,000 in cash and gambling chips with a face value of around HK$80,000. Police estimated the five venues generated up to HK$1 million a month in combined profit.

Police said the syndicate recruited young people via messaging apps and social settings for quick cash, paying HK$500 to HK$800 to subcontract debt-collection tasks that included splashing red paint, harassing calls and WhatsApp threats. Some of those arrested had registered SIM cards with their personal details for use in threatening calls. A police spokesman warned young people against the temptation of fast cash from criminal groups and advised parents to monitor sudden changes in their children’s spending or friendships. Criminal damage and criminal intimidation carry maximum penalties of 10 and five years’ imprisonment respectively. Police said the operation had severely disrupted the triad faction’s income sources and that inquiries continue.

zh.headline: 警搗破三合會放數集團拘57人 包括14歲少年
zh.dek: 警方瓦解一個三合會操控的非法追債集團，並搗破一間色情場所、一所毒窟及三個非法賭場，部分被捕者年紀僅十多歲。
body: 香港警方在七月進行特別行動，搗破一個活躍全港、由三合會操控的非法追債集團，拘捕57名年齡介乎14至70歲的男女，並搗破相關非法場所。
行動於7月13日在秀茂坪邨展開埋伏，截獲一名14歲少年，當時他身上帶有一瓶紅油及指虎。他涉嫌管有意圖損壞財產物品及管有違禁武器被捕。其後數日，包括數名15至18歲核心成員在內的人士，因涉嫌串謀刑事毀壞及與區內多宗案件有關而被捕。
7月22至28日期間，警方再拘10人，涉及另外10宗刑事毀壞及恐嚇案件。7月28至30日聯合行動搗破五個非法場所，再拘41人，涉及經營色情場所、經營毒窟、販運及吸食毒品，以及非法賭博等罪行。檢獲可卡因、冰毒、賭博機、麻雀枱、撲克枱、約4萬元現金及面值約8萬元的籌碼。警方估計該五個場所每月合共賺取高達100萬元利潤。
警方表示，集團透過即時通訊軟件及社交場合招募年輕人，以500至800元報酬外判追債工作，手法包括潑紅油、滋擾電話及WhatsApp恐嚇。部分被捕者更用個人資料登記電話卡供集團發出恐嚇訊息。警方發言人警告青少年切勿貪圖快錢而墮入犯罪集團圈套，並呼籲家長留意子女突然增加的開支或交友情況。刑事毀壞及刑事恐嚇最高可判監10年及5年。警方指行動已嚴重打擊該三合會派系收入來源，調查仍在進行。
